EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by two strong C-H stretching bands at 2878 / 2952 cm⁻¹, indicating a saturated aliphatic molecule.  
The most diagnostic feature is the very intense Raman line at 923 cm⁻¹.  A strong Raman-active band in the 920–930 cm⁻¹ region is characteristic of the symmetric ring-breathing (C–C stretch) mode of a cyclopropane ring; this vibration is known to be one of the most intense lines in cyclopropane derivatives.  Peaks at 880 cm⁻¹ and 818 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to additional ring deformations of the strained three-membered ring, while bands at 1057 cm⁻¹ and 1243 cm⁻¹ correspond to CH₂ rocking / C–C stretches and C–O stretches of an aliphatic alcohol, respectively.  The weak 1450 cm⁻¹ band matches the CH₂/CH₃ bending expected for saturated chains.  

Among the ten candidates, only candidate 1, “CCC1(C)CC1CCO”, contains a cyclopropane ring together with a short aliphatic chain and a terminal alcohol – a structural combination that accounts for all observed bands.  None of the other candidates has a three-membered ring, making them unlikely to give the very strong 923 cm⁻¹ feature.
